questions.question: If your brakes fail going downhill, why should you decide what to do quickly?

options.text: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
The longer you wait, the more vehicles will get out of your way.
The longer you wait, the slower your vehicle will go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
questions.explanation: When your brakes fail on a downhill slope, act quickly. The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle moves and the harder it becomes to stop.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, a bus driver should:

options.text: Stop the bus 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track.
Drive carefully, but only stop if a train is coming.
Speed up so the bus has enough momentum to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the bus 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track.
questions.explanation: When approaching a railroad crossing, stop your bus 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track. Look both ways for trains. Do not proceed until you are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: During the driving test, when asked to change lanes:

options.text: You do not need to worry about other drivers.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes as quickly as possible, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes during a driving test, check your mirrors, use your turn signal, and smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: ____ is a thin, clear layer of ice on road surfaces.

options.text: White ice
Black ice
Green ice

questions.correctAnswerText: Black ice
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road underneath it. Black ice may look like a wet road instead of ice. Watch for black ice when roads look wet and the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: Why is texting while driving especially dangerous?

options.text: It takes your attention away from the road and requires you to take your hands off the wheel.
A message may upset the driver.
People may become too focused on their phones.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your attention away from the road and requires you to take your hands off the wheel.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous because it is both a mental and physical distraction. It takes your focus off the road and requires you to remove at least one hand from the steering wheel.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: You should not use your mirrors.
You should use your mirrors.
You should not use your turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should use your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signals and check your mirrors when changing lanes.

questions.question: If you are transporting a drunk passenger, you should:

options.text: Force them to exit the bus immediately.
Wait until you reach a safe place, like a scheduled stop or well-lit area, before having them exit.
Give them coffee to help them sober up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you reach a safe place, like a scheduled stop or well-lit area, before having them exit.
questions.explanation: You are responsible for a drunk passenger's safety. Let them exit at a safe location, such as the next scheduled stop or a well-lit area where other people are present.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system can:

options.text: Let poisonous fumes into the cab.
Improve fuel efficiency.
Make steering more difficult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let poisonous fumes into the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous because poisonous fumes can enter the cab.

questions.question: Without engine oil:

options.text: A vehicle will use less fuel.
An engine can be destroyed quickly.
An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) will not work properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: An engine can be destroyed quickly.
questions.explanation: Engine oil is critical. Without it, an engine can be destroyed very quickly.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Look both ways but do not stop.
Stop and get out of the bus to look for a train.
Stop before the tracks and look both ways before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before the tracks and look both ways before proceeding.
questions.explanation: Stop your bus 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track. Look and listen for trains. Only proceed when you are certain no trains are coming. You do not need to stop at streetcar crossings, when a police officer is directing traffic, at green traffic signals, or at crossings marked as exempt or abandoned.

questions.question: One way to prevent fatigue on long trips is to:

options.text: Take frequent breaks.
Text while driving.
Drink caffeine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent breaks.
questions.explanation: Take a break every 100 miles or every two hours of driving to avoid fatigue. Driving at night or when you would normally be sleeping is very dangerous.

questions.question: ____ are the most likely to be affected by strong winds.

options.text: Light vehicles
Heavy vehicles
Vehicles with open windows

questions.correctAnswerText: Light vehicles
questions.explanation: Strong winds make it harder to control a vehicle. Light vehicles are affected much more than heavy vehicles.

questions.question: As part of the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Explain why you must check the items you are checking.
Change the coolant.
Replace a headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain why you must check the items you are checking.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection. You will need to explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Always use turn signals when changing lanes.
Only use turn signals if there is a vehicle next to them.
Not use a turn signal if a lane change is obvious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: If making a tight turn, the operator of a CMV should:

options.text: Be able to drive as fast as the driver of a car.
Not be concerned about speed, but focus on the road.
Warn drivers behind by braking early and slowing gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn drivers behind by braking early and slowing gradually.
questions.explanation: Drivers behind you may not know how slowly a CMV must go for a tight turn. Brake early and slow down gradually to warn them in advance.

questions.question: When should mirrors be adjusted?

options.text: Before driving
While driving
After driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Before driving
questions.explanation: Check mirrors before you start driving. If you have a trailer, it must be straight so mirrors are adjusted correctly.

questions.question: After an accident, flares should be used with caution because:

options.text: There may be fuel spilled on the ground that could catch fire.
Other drivers may not see the flares if the weather is sunny.
Flares are expensive.

questions.correctAnswerText: There may be fuel spilled on the ground that could catch fire.
questions.explanation: Spilled fuel can catch fire if flares are used nearby. Be careful when using flares after an accident.

questions.question: What does the vehicle inspection report do?

options.text: Inform the motor carrier about problems that may need fixing
Ensure that the vehicle is inspected regularly
Keep people accountable for inspecting the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Inform the motor carrier about problems that may need fixing
questions.explanation: The vehicle inspection report tells the carrier about any problems that need to be fixed.

questions.question: Vehicles driving behind a truck:

options.text: May have difficulty seeing objects in front of the truck.
Often have a great view of the roadway in front of them.
Do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have difficulty seeing objects in front of the truck.
questions.explanation: Your truck may block the view of drivers behind you. They may not see hazards ahead. Flash your brakes and warn other drivers before you slow down or stop.

questions.question: The use of a hand-held mobile device while driving is:

options.text: Prohibited.
Acceptable if weather conditions are clear.
Permitted if use is work-related.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prohibited.
questions.explanation: Using a hand-held mobile phone while driving a CMV is illegal and dangerous.
